title: Anchored fragment index and sticky-slot reclaimer for cross-request prompt reuse
creator: Aisha Kumar
description:
Problem: Inter-request reuse for leading-context fragments is limited by fragmentation and noisy eviction on GPU slab allocators. Existing content-addressed fragment approaches reduce duplication but don't account for temporal locality, tenant stickiness, or slab fragmentation, causing spiky reclaim behavior and unexpected OOMs under mixed workloads.

Goal: Build an "anchored fragment index" plus a "sticky-slot reclaimer" that improves reuse of prompt fragments across requests while reducing slab fragmentation and variance in allocator behavior. The anchored index maps canonical fragment fingerprints to one or more 'anchors' (slot reservations) with metadata for recency, tenant affinity, and eviction cost. The sticky-slot reclaimer will gently reclaim inactive anchors based on age, working-set pressure, and tenant priority rather than immediate eviction, enabling predictable latency and lower peak memory.

This ticket covers design and prototype implementation of the index and reclaimer in the serving runtime, integration points with the scheduler (for placement hints), and end-to-end validation with synthetic interleaved workloads. It includes metrics, safety gates, rollout plan, and a follow-up plan to surface telemetry in Console.
acceptance_criteria: Anchored fragment index persisted in GPU-local metadata with O(1) lookup per fingerprints and <2µs median lookup overhead in microbenchmarks
Sticky-slot reclaimer reclaims anchors gradually and reduces 95th percentile memory spikes by >=30% on our mixed multi-tenant replay (baseline: current mainline)
No increase in median token latency >5% for standard small- and medium-sequence workloads on test fleet
Feature controlled by runtime flag (runtime.feature.anchored_fragments) and safe rollback path documented
Integration tests that simulate tenant churn, cold starts, and prolonged single-tenant bursts with assertions on memory stability and correct fragment reuse
steps: Design anchored index data model (fingerprint -> list of anchors). anchors store: slot_id, tenant_hint, last_access_ts, reuse_count, eviction_weight
Implement compact on-GPU index (linear-probed hash table) with CPU mirror for reconciliation and persistent checkpointing during scale events
Add allocation API to mark slots as 'anchored' and annotate allocator to prefer placing requested fragments into anchors when present
Implement sticky-slot reclaimer: multi-heuristic policy (age, tenant_affinity_score, global_memory_pressure, predicted_reuse) and exponential backoff to avoid thrashing
Integrate with scheduler/placement to surface anchor hints and honor tenant priority (Dedicated vs Hosted tiers)
Add telemetry: anchor hit/miss counters, reclaimed anchors per minute, median reclaim latency, memory spike delta per pod
Run canary on synthetic mixed-tenant replay (10k reqs/s) and compare against baseline memory and latency curves
Iterate on heuristics and tune thresholds; prepare rollout with small % of traffic and monitor dashboards
Document behavior in Confluence and mark as experimental until 2 canary rounds pass
comments: 2026-02-11 Aisha: Kickoff - aligned with product (PM Nora) and infra (Raj). Confirmed goal is to reduce fragmentation-related spikes while improving cross-request fragment reuse. Agreed to keep feature behind runtime flag.

2026-02-18 Liam: Prototype of compact GPU index pushed to branch feat/anchored-index. Index uses 64-bit fragment fingerprint and stores anchor entries as 32-bit slot IDs + 32-bit metadata bitfield. Microbenchmarks show ~1.6µs lookup on A100-40GB (single-threaded). Link: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/4021

2026-02-24 Raj: Reviewed allocator integration notes. Concern: allocator currently packs slabs aggressively; need safe ordering so reclamation does not race with active batch writes. Added 'anchor-pin' handshake between index and allocator.

2026-03-02 QA: First synthetic workload run with 5 tenants interleaved. Observed 22% reduction in 95th memory usage but a small spike of reclaim latency up to 45ms under burst. Hypothesis: backoff parameters too small. Added tuning ticket for reclaim backoff (follow-up).

2026-03-05 PM Nora: Product review - asked for tenant-priority awareness to be explicit so Dedicated customers are less likely to lose anchors. Decided to surface tenant tier as part of anchor metadata and config knobs in Dedicated clusters.

2026-03-08 Security (Maya): Confirmed no increase in cross-tenant data exposure as anchors store only fingerprints and allocator slot IDs; requested documentation to show non-reconstructability of raw prompt text from index entries. Added security_review_required label.

2026-03-10 Liam: Performance tuning complete for default heuristic set. Canary rollout plan prepared (see links). Ready for initial canary on 5% of hosted realtime traffic next week under feature flag.
risks: Reclaimer misconfiguration could cause increased latency if anchors are reclaimed aggressively during bursts
Allocator races if handshake not respected — could cause double-free assertions in rare interleaves
Telemetry gaps may delay detection of regressions; need consoles added before broad rollout
rollout_plan: Stage 1: Internal cluster tests and synthetic replay (done). Stage 2: 5% hosted realtime canary under flag (2 days, automated rollbacks). Stage 3: 25% with Dedicated cluster opt-in. Stage 4: Default enabled for new deployments once 72h stability observed.
next_steps: Run 5% canary for 48h and validate memory spike reduction and latency SLOs
Add automatic rollback trigger based on reclaim-latency>100ms or memory-spike regression>10%
Create follow-up ticket to expose anchor heuristics in Console and add per-tenant reclaim metrics
Coordinate with Support for potential customer questions during canary
